questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The office created a separate line for students who only needed to turn in forms. This kept those students from waiting behind people with longer questions. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported by the passage?

answer.text: The office stopped accepting forms from students.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says students turned in forms.

answer.text: The separate line helped students with simple tasks finish more quickly.

feedback.text: Correct. The line was for turning in forms, so students did not wait behind longer questions.

answer.text: Students with longer questions were not allowed in the office.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not say anyone was not allowed.

answer.text: The office line became longer because forms were removed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says the separate line reduced waiting for some students.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The drama club practiced scene changes with a timer. Members learned which props could be moved together so the stage would be ready faster. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The timer helped the club improve scene changes"?

answer.text: The drama club had members.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show improvement.

answer.text: The props were on a stage.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names the place but does not support the result.

answer.text: The club practiced drama.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general to support the paraphrase.

answer.text: Members learned which props could be moved together.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains how timing helped them improve the process.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The math teacher posted solved sample problems beside the homework bin. Students checked the samples before submitting work and corrected simple mistakes. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported by the passage?

answer.text: Sample problems helped students review their work before turning it in.

feedback.text: Correct. The samples let students check and correct work before submitting.

answer.text: The homework bin caused students to make more mistakes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says students corrected mistakes.

answer.text: The teacher stopped giving homework because students used samples.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not say homework stopped.

answer.text: Students copied sample problems instead of doing homework.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says students checked samples and corrected mistakes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The school nurse added posters about handwashing near the water fountains. The posters reminded students to use soap and scrub long enough before returning to class. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The posters reminded students how to wash hands properly"?

answer.text: The posters were near the water fountains.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives location but not the handwashing instructions.

answer.text: The school had a nurse.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not prove what the posters taught.

answer.text: The posters reminded students to use soap and scrub long enough.

feedback.text: Correct. This evidence directly supports the paraphrase.

answer.text: Students returned to class.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain proper handwashing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The robotics team kept notes after each test run. The notes helped members remember which wheel settings worked best on carpet and tile. Question: Which paraphrase is most accurate?

answer.text: The team's notes helped members track which robot settings worked on different surfaces.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the main idea and important details.

answer.text: The team stopped testing because notes made the robot work perfectly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not say testing stopped or that the robot was perfect.

answer.text: The notes replaced the robot during competitions.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Notes helped the team remember settings; they did not replace the robot.

answer.text: Members used carpet and tile because they did not take notes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says they did take notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The cafeteria labeled the spicy foods on the lunch menu. Students could choose meals more confidently because they knew which items matched their preferences. Question: Which evidence supports the paraphrase "The labels helped students make food choices"?

answer.text: The cafeteria served lunch.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show how labels helped students choose.

answer.text: Some foods were spicy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fact from the passage but does not fully support the paraphrase.

answer.text: The menu existed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The menu alone does not prove the labels helped.

answer.text: Students could choose meals more confidently.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the idea that labels helped students decide.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The history teacher showed a timeline before assigning the chapter. The timeline helped students see which events happened before the war and which happened after it. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported?

answer.text: The timeline replaced the chapter because students did not need to read.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says the timeline was shown before the chapter.

answer.text: The timeline helped students understand the order of events around the war.

feedback.text: Correct. The timeline showed what happened before and after the war.

answer.text: The teacher assigned the chapter after the war ended.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This confuses the historical event with the class activity.

answer.text: The war happened because students used a timeline.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not supported by the passage.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The debate coach asked students to underline the sentence that best supported each claim. This helped speakers avoid using details that sounded interesting but did not prove their point. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The coach wanted students to choose relevant evidence"?

answer.text: The students were on a debate team.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show the evidence habit.

answer.text: Some details sounded interesting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Interesting details may not be relevant.

answer.text: The coach asked students to underline the sentence that best supported each claim.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports choosing relevant evidence.

answer.text: Speakers had points.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The field trip group reviewed the museum map before leaving school. By planning the route, the group made sure it had enough time for the science exhibit and the history exhibit. Question: Which paraphrase is most accurate?

answer.text: The group skipped the museum because the map was too difficult.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says they planned a route.

answer.text: The museum map showed only the history exhibit.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage mentions science and history exhibits.

answer.text: The field trip group left the map at school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says they reviewed the map before leaving.

answer.text: The group used the map to plan enough time for two museum exhibits.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the action and purpose accurately.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The student council tested two announcement formats. More students remembered the message when it was shown as a short video instead of read only over the speaker. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The video announcement was more effective"?

answer.text: More students remembered the message when it was shown as a short video.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the paraphrase.

answer.text: The student council tested two formats.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This shows a test happened but not which format worked better.

answer.text: The announcement was read over the speaker.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is one format but does not show effectiveness.

answer.text: The student council had a message.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The teacher placed extra pencils in a cup beside the door. Students who forgot supplies could take one quickly without interrupting the beginning of class. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported?

answer.text: The teacher removed pencils because students interrupted class.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The teacher added pencils.

answer.text: Students had to leave class to find supplies.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says students could take pencils quickly.

answer.text: Extra pencils near the door helped students get supplies without disrupting class.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning and important details.

answer.text: The beginning of class was canceled because pencils were missing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not say class was canceled.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The school added arrows on the hallway floor during construction. The arrows showed students which path avoided the closed staircase. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The arrows helped students navigate around construction"?

answer.text: The school had hallways.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show how students navigated.

answer.text: The arrows showed students which path avoided the closed staircase.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the paraphrase.

answer.text: Construction existed at the school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives context but not how arrows helped.

answer.text: The staircase was closed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains the problem, but the arrows are what helped students navigate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The music director recorded each section of the song separately. Students could listen to their own section at home and practice the notes that matched their part. Question: Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: Separate recordings helped students practice the exact music for their section.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the main idea accurately.

answer.text: Students stopped practicing because the director recorded the song.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The recordings supported practice.

answer.text: The music director deleted the students' parts from the song.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says each section was recorded.

answer.text: Students listened to unrelated songs at home.

feedback.text: Incorrect. They listened to their own section.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: A community group placed benches along the walking trail. Older walkers said the benches made the trail easier to use because they could rest between longer sections. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The benches made the trail more accessible for older walkers"?

answer.text: The group was from the community.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support accessibility.

answer.text: The walking trail had sections.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail alone does not prove the benches helped.

answer.text: The benches were placed outside.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

answer.text: Older walkers could rest between longer sections.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the paraphrase.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The technology teacher gave students a checklist before they submitted slides. The checklist reminded them to use readable fonts, correct spelling, and images related to the topic. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported?

answer.text: The teacher asked students to avoid images in every slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says images should be related to the topic.

answer.text: Students submitted slides before receiving the checklist.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The checklist came before submission.

answer.text: The checklist helped students review slides for readability, spelling, and relevant images.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately restates the purpose of the checklist.

answer.text: The checklist replaced the slide presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It helped students review slides.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The principal moved the lost-and-found table near the cafeteria. More students checked it during lunch because they passed the table on the way to eat. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "Moving the table helped students notice the lost-and-found"?

answer.text: The principal moved the table.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This tells what happened but not why it helped students notice it.

answer.text: More students checked it during lunch.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the idea that more students noticed and used it.

answer.text: The cafeteria served lunch.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is background, not evidence of the result.

answer.text: Students had lost items.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not focus on what items were lost.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The science club shared plant care cards with each classroom. The cards listed watering days and sunlight needs so students would know how to keep the plants healthy. Question: Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: The science club removed plants because students forgot watering days.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says the club shared cards.

answer.text: Students kept plants in sunlight so the cards would stay healthy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This confuses the cards with the plants.

answer.text: Plant care cards helped students understand how to care for classroom plants.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the action and purpose accurate.

answer.text: The cards listed classroom rules instead of plant needs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The cards listed watering days and sunlight needs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The coach posted the practice plan before warm-ups. Players knew which stations they would visit, so the team spent less time waiting for directions. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The practice plan helped the team use time better"?

answer.text: The team spent less time waiting for directions.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the paraphrase.

answer.text: The coach posted something.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague.

answer.text: Players did warm-ups.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not prove the plan saved time.

answer.text: The stations existed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail alone does not show improved time use.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The local animal shelter created adoption cards for each pet. The cards described the pet's age, habits, and favorite activities so visitors could learn about animals before meeting them. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported?

answer.text: Visitors adopted animals without reading any information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says cards gave information before meetings.

answer.text: The shelter used cards to help visitors learn about pets before meeting them.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately restates the purpose of the cards.

answer.text: The cards replaced the animals at the shelter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The cards described animals.

answer.text: The shelter stopped visitors from meeting pets.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Visitors could learn before meeting them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The school added bike racks near the gym entrance. Students who rode bikes no longer had to lock them to trees far from the building. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The bike racks gave riders a better place to secure bikes"?

answer.text: The school had a gym.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support the bike-rack purpose.

answer.text: Some students rode bikes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives background but not the improvement.

answer.text: The entrance was near the gym.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is location only.

answer.text: Students no longer had to lock bikes to trees far from the building.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows how the racks improved where students secured bikes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The newspaper club added captions below every photograph. Readers said the captions helped them understand who was pictured and why the moment mattered. Question: Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: Captions helped readers understand the people and importance of each photograph.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the main idea accurately.

answer.text: Captions made readers ignore the photographs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Captions helped readers understand photos.

answer.text: The newspaper club removed photos because captions were confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The club added captions below photos.

answer.text: Readers wrote captions because the newspaper club did not know who was pictured.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The club added the captions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The counselor made a chart showing application deadlines for clubs and programs. Students used the chart to plan which forms needed to be completed first. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The chart helped students organize deadlines"?

answer.text: The counselor made a chart.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is the action but not the result.

answer.text: Clubs and programs existed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives context but not how the chart helped.

answer.text: Students used the chart to plan which forms needed to be completed first.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the paraphrase.

answer.text: Some forms had deadlines.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains why a chart might be needed, but not that it helped.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The teacher put vocabulary cards beside the reading passage. Students used the cards to understand difficult words before answering questions. Question: Which paraphrase is best supported?

answer.text: Students answered questions before reading any words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The cards helped before answering.

answer.text: The teacher removed the reading passage.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage remained with vocabulary cards beside it.

answer.text: Vocabulary cards made the passage impossible to read.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The cards helped students understand the passage.

answer.text: Vocabulary cards helped students understand difficult words in the passage.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately restates the purpose of the cards.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The park placed distance markers along the running path. Runners could check how far they had gone without using a phone or watch. Question: Which evidence best supports the paraphrase "The markers helped runners track distance"?

answer.text: The park had a path.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not prove that runners tracked distance.

answer.text: Runners could check how far they had gone.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the paraphrase.

answer.text: Some runners had phones.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says runners did not need phones or watches.

answer.text: The markers were along a path.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives location but not the result.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U01_L03_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.10

Passage: The teacher asked groups to write their discussion question at the top of the paper. This helped every answer stay connected to the same focus. Question: Which paraphrase is most accurate?

answer.text: Writing the question helped groups keep their answers focused.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the purpose of writing the question.

answer.text: Groups erased the question so answers would be longer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage says they wrote the question.

answer.text: The paper replaced the group discussion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The passage does not say discussion stopped.

answer.text: Every answer changed focus because the question was missing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The question helped answers stay connected.
